# graphforge-api

GraphForge public Rust API — the GraphForge engine facade.

This crate is an internal layer of [GraphForge](https://graphforge.sh), a Rust
graph engine with Arrow results and Parquet storage. Most applications should
start with one of these entry points:

- Rust: [`graphforge-api`](https://crates.io/crates/graphforge-api), the public engine facade.
- Terminal: `gf`, installed from [`graphforge-cli`](https://crates.io/crates/graphforge-cli).
- Python: the [`graphforge` wheel](https://pypi.org/project/graphforge/).
- Node: [`@curatelabs/graphforge`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@curatelabs/graphforge).

Use matching versions across the engine and bindings. Before v1.0.0, GraphForge
does not guarantee backward compatibility or project migration.

## Quickstart

Create a Rust binary with `cargo new my-graph` and enter its directory. Add
`graphforge-api` at the version shown on this crate page (replace `<version>`):

```sh
cargo add graphforge-api@<version>
```

Replace `src/main.rs` with:

```rust
use graphforge_api::GraphForge;

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let graph = GraphForge::new(None)?;
    graph.execute("CREATE (:Person {name: 'Alice'})")?;
    let result = graph.execute("MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p.name AS name")?;
    for batch in result.batches {
        println!("{batch:?}");
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

Run `cargo run`. This example uses the full engine in memory; its data lasts
only for this process. Query results are Arrow record batches.
